english.ad_mitsubishi_b2m_equipment_1_desc: The Mitsubishi B2M1 was a carrier torpedo bomber designed in the 1920's.
english.ad_mitsubishi_ki_20_equipment_1_desc: The Mitsubishi Ki-20 was a four-engine heavy bomber liscense built from the Junkers K.51, a militarised version of an airliner.
english.ad_mitsubishi_t92_scout_equipment_1_desc: A plane developed specifically for photo reconnaissance. Relies primarily on speed and stealth to survive and will generally lose in any stand-up fight.
english.ad_nakajima_a2n_equipment_1_desc: The Nakajima A2N is a carrier fighter aircraft.
english.ad_hiro_h4h_equipment_1_desc: The Hiro H4H is a long-range flying boat.
english.ad_mitsubishi_b2m_equipment_2_desc: The Mitsubishi B2M2 was an improved production variant with reduced wingspan and modified tail from the B2M1 carrier torpedo bomber.
english.ad_mitsubishi_ki_1_equipment_1_desc: The Mitsubishi Ki-1 was a twin-engined bomber.
english.ad_mitsubishi_ki_2_equipment_1_desc: The Mitsubishi Ki-2 was a pre-war light bomber.
english.ad_aichi_d1a_equipment_1_desc: The Aichi D1A1 was a carrier dive-bomber developed from an imported Heinkel He 66.
english.ad_kawasaki_ki_3_equipment_1_desc: The Kawasaki Ki-3 was a biplane light bomber.
english.ad_mitsubishi_ki_2_equipment_2_desc: The Mitsubishi Ki-2-II was a pre-war light bomber.
english.ad_nakajima_ki_4_equipment_1_desc: The Nakajima Ki-4 was a reconnaissance and close air support biplane.
english.ad_yokosuka_b3y_equipment_1_desc: The Yokosuka B3Y was a carrier torpedo bomber designed in the early 1930's.
english.ad_aichi_d1a_equipment_2_desc: The Aichi D1A2 was a carrier dive-bomber developed from an imported Heinkel He 66.
english.ad_kawasaki_ki_10_equipment_1_desc: The Kawasaki Ki-10 was a biplane fighter designed for the Japanese Army. It was chosen for its high manoeuvrability.
english.ad_mitsubishi_g3m_equipment_1_desc: The Mitsubishi G3M was a long-range naval bomber designed for the Japanese Navy.
english.ad_mitsubishi_ki_1_equipment_2_desc: The Mitsubishi Ki-1-II was a twin-engined bomber.
english.ad_nakajima_a2n_equipment_2_desc: The Nakajima A4N is a carrier fighter aircraft.
english.ad_kawasaki_ki_10_equipment_2_desc: The Kawasaki Ki-10 KAI addressed major stability issues and improved the engine cowling.
english.ad_mitsubishi_a5m_equipment_1_desc: The Mitsubishi A5M is a carrier fighter aircraft.
english.ad_yokosuka_b4y_equipment_1_desc: The Yokosuka B4Y was a carrier torpedo bomber.
english.ad_kawanishi_h6k_equipment_1_desc: The Kawanishi H6K is a long-range flying boat.
english.ad_mitsubishi_ki_15_scout_equipment_1_de: A plane developed specifically for photo reconnaissance. Relies primarily on speed and stealth to survive and will generally lose in any stand-up fight.
english.ad_nakajima_b5n_equipment_1_desc: The Nakajima B5N1 was a carrier torpedo bomber. The aircraft suffered issues with reliability and lack of power in its early stages.
english.ad_nakajima_ki_27_equipment_1_desc: The Nakajima Ki-27 was a light fighter aircraft.
english.ad_a7he_equipment_1_desc: Heinkel's competitor to the Bf 109. This is the Japanese Navy version.
english.ad_kawasaki_ki_32_equipment_1_desc: The Kawasaki Ki-32 was a light bomber aircraft. Although its performance was superior to the competing Mitsubishi Ki-30, engine problems resulted in both types entering production.
english.ad_mitsubishi_a5m_equipment_2_desc: The Mitsubishi A5M4 is a carrier fighter aircraft.
english.ad_mitsubishi_g3m_equipment_2_desc: The Mitsubishi G3M2 was a long-range naval bomber designed for the Japanese Navy.
english.ad_mitsubishi_ki_21_equipment_1_desc: The Mitsubishi Ki-21 was a twin-engined bomber.
english.ad_mitsubishi_ki_30_equipment_1_desc: The Mitsubishi Ki-30 was a light bomber aircraft. Although its performance was inferior to the competing Kawasaki Ki-32, the Ki-30 was much more reliable and both entered production.
english.ad_tachikawa_ki_36_equipment_1_desc: The Tachikawa Ki-36 was designed to provide air support for the Japanese army.
english.ad_aichi_d3a_equipment_1_desc: The Aichi D3A was a carrier dive-bomber aircraft.
english.ad_axhe_equipment_1_desc: The Heinkel He 100 is a high-speed development of the He 112. It is a fast light fighter aircraft. This is the Japanese Navy version.
english.ad_kawanishi_h6k_equipment_2_desc: The Kawanishi H6K4 is a long-range flying boat.
english.ad_mitsubishi_ki_15_scout_equipment_2_de: A plane developed specifically for photo reconnaissance. Relies primarily on speed and stealth to survive and will generally lose in any stand-up fight.
english.ad_nakajima_b5n_equipment_2_desc: The Nakajima B5N2 was a carrier torpedo bomber. This was a development of the B5N1 with a more powerful engine, solving most of the issues of the earlier model.
english.ad_kawasaki_ki_45_equipment_1_desc: The Kawasaki Ki-45 was a twin engine fighter based on the design of the Ki-38. However, the Japanese Army initially showed little interest in the project and only 11 were built.
english.ad_kawasaki_ki_48_equipment_1_desc: The Kawasaki Ki-48 was a light bomber aircraft developed in response to the performance of the Soviet Tupolev SB-2's in Chinese hands during the second Sino-Japanese war.
english.ad_mitsubishi_ki_21_equipment_2_desc: The Mitsubishi Ki-21-II was a twin-engined bomber.
english.ad_mitsubishi_ki_51_equipment_1_desc: The Mitsubishi Ki-51 was a ground attack aircraft designed from the Ki-30 bomber.
english.ad_nakajima_ki_43_equipment_1_desc: The Nakajima Ki-43 was a light fighter aircraft. It was the first model of the Ki-43 series, which would become the most numerous aircraft in the IJA during World War 2.
english.ad_kawanishi_h8k_equipment_1_desc: The Kawanishi H8K is a long-range flying boat.
english.ad_mitsubishi_a6m_equipment_1_desc: The Mitsubishi A6M Reisen, or Zero, was an iconic Japanese carrier fighter.
english.ad_mitsubishi_g4m_equipment_1_desc: The Mitsubishi G4M was a long-range naval bomber designed for the Japanese Navy.
english.ad_mitsubishi_ki_46_scout_equipment_1_de: A plane developed specifically for photo reconnaissance. Relies primarily on speed and stealth to survive and will generally lose in any stand-up fight.
english.ad_nakajima_ki_43_equipment_2_desc: The Nakajima Ki-43-II was a light fighter aircraft. It was an improvement of the Ki-43, and the most numerous aircraft in the IJA during World War 2.
english.ad_nakajima_ki_44_equipment_1_desc: The Nakajima Ki-44 'Shoki' was designed for a high speed and fast climbing fighter interceptor. It was the fastest Japanese fighter upon entering service.
english.ad_nakajima_ki_49_equipment_1_desc: The Nakajima Ki-49 was a twin-engined bomber, well liked for its defensive armament and armor.
english.ad_kawasaki_ki_45_kai_equipment_1_desc: The Kawasaki Ki-45 KAI was a redesign of the Ki-45 airframe to improve its performance. It saw a variety of different armaments fitted to it in efforts to perfect a bomber killer.
english.ad_kawasaki_ki_48_equipment_2_desc: The Kawasaki Ki-48-II saw the Ki-48 redesigned to use more powerful engines and improve flight stability. It also featured a larger bombload and additional armor.
english.ad_kawasaki_ki_61_equipment_1_desc: The Kawasaki Ki-61 was a fighter aircraft powered by a liscense built Daimler-Benz DB-601A engine. It carried more armor than earlier Japanese fighters.
english.ad_mansyu_ki_71_equipment_1_desc: The Mansyu Ki-71 was a modernized version of the Ki-51.
english.ad_mitsubishi_a6m3_equipment_1_desc: The Mitsubishi A6M3 Reisen was a development of the A6M2.
english.ad_mitsubishi_j2m_equipment_1_desc: The Mitsubishi J2M was a land-based fighter designed for the Japanese Navy. It had a heavy armament and good flight performance.
english.ad_nakajima_g5n_equipment_1_desc: Based off of a rejected American airliner, the Nakajima G5N Shinzan was a four-engined bomber developed for the Japanese navy. The poor performance of the prototypes lead to them being converted to transports.
english.ad_nakajima_j1n_equipment_1_desc: The Nakajima J1N Gekko was a reconnaissance and escort aircraft designed to protect Japanese bombers flying deep into enemy territory. It is a night fighter.
english.ad_nakajima_ki_44_equipment_2_desc: The Nakajima Ki-44-II 'Shoki' was designed for a high speed and fast climbing fighter interceptor.
english.ad_nakajima_ki_49_equipment_2_desc: The Nakajima Ki-49-II was a twin-engined bomber, well liked for its defensive armament and armor.
english.ad_yokosuka_d4y_equipment_1_desc: The Yokosuka D4Y Suisei was a carrier dive-bomber aircraft.
english.ad_yokosuka_d4y_scout_equipment_1_desc: A plane developed specifically for photo reconnaissance. Relies primarily on speed and stealth to survive and will generally lose in any stand-up fight.
english.ad_kawanishi_h8k_equipment_2_desc: The Kawanishi H8K2 is a long-range flying boat.
english.ad_kawanishi_n1k1j_equipment_1_desc: The Kawanishi N1K1-J was a land-based fighter designed for the Japanese Navy. It was developed from the N1K1 floatplane.
english.ad_kawasaki_ki_61_equipment_2_desc: The Kawasaki Ki-61-II KAI was a development of the Ki-61 fitted with a more powerful engine optimized for high-altitude operations.
english.ad_mitsubishi_g4m2_equipment_1_desc: The Mitsubishi G4M2 was a development of the G4M1 that featured better flight performance and heavier armament.
english.ad_mitsubishi_ki_46_scout_equipment_2_de: A plane developed specifically for photo reconnaissance. Relies primarily on speed and stealth to survive and will generally lose in any stand-up fight.
english.ad_nakajima_b6n_equipment_1_desc: The Nakajima B6N Tenzan was a carrier torpdeo bomber.
english.ad_nakajima_ki_43_equipment_3_desc: The Nakajima Ki-43-III was a light fighter aircraft. It was the final evolution of the Ki-43 series.
english.ad_aichi_b7a_equipment_1_desc: The Aichi B7A Ryusei was a carrier bomber that was capable of both diving attacks, as well as torpedo attacks.
english.ad_kawanishi_n1k2j_equipment_1_desc: The Kawanishi N1K2-J was a land-based fighter designed for the Japanese Navy. It was developed from the N1K1-J and was intended to ease maintenance and manufacturing.
english.ad_kawasaki_ki_102_equipment_1_desc: The Kawasaki Ki-102a was a heavy fighter developed from the Ki-45 line of aircraft. The Ki-102a variant was intended primarily as a heavy fighter for bomber interception.
english.ad_kawasaki_ki_102_equipment_2_desc: The Kawasaki Ki-102b was a heavy fighter developed from the Ki-45 line of aircraft. The Ki-102b variant was intended for ground attack and anti-shipping attack.
english.ad_mitsubishi_a6m5c_equipment_1_desc: The Mitsubishi A6M5c Reisen was a later development of the A6M, using the Sakae 21 engine.
english.ad_mitsubishi_a6m7_equipment_1_desc: The Mitsubishi A6M7 was a derivative of the A6M Reisen designed to operate from aircraft carriers as a fighter-bomber.
english.ad_mitsubishi_g4m2_gb_equipment_1_desc: The Mitsubishi G4M2e was a version of the G4M designed to carry the Ohka, a manned suicide missile.
english.ad_mitsubishi_j2m_equipment_2_desc: The Mitsubishi J2M5 was a land-based fighter designed for the Japanese Navy. It had a heavy armament and good flight performance.
english.ad_mitsubishi_ki_67_equipment_1_desc: The Ki-67 was a highly maneuverable twin-engined bomber.
english.ad_nakajima_c6n_scout_equipment_1_desc: A plane developed specifically for photo reconnaissance. Relies primarily on speed and stealth to survive and will generally lose in any stand-up fight.
english.ad_nakajima_g8n_equipment_1_desc: The Nakajima G8N Renzan was a long range four-engined bomber designed for the Japanese Navy. Lack of materials and changing priorities kept the aircraft from being put into production.
english.ad_nakajima_j5n_equipment_1_desc: The Nakajima J5N Tenrai was a twin engine night fighter based on the earlier J1N.
english.ad_nakajima_ki_44_equipment_3_desc: The Nakajima Ki-44-III 'Shoki' was designed for a high speed and fast climbing fighter interceptor.
english.ad_nakajima_ki_84_equipment_1_desc: The Nakajima Ki-84 was designed as an all-purpose fighter.
english.ad_yokosuka_d4y_equipment_2_desc: The Yokosuka D4Y3 Suisei was a modification of the D4Y to use a radial engine.
english.ad_yokosuka_p1_equipment_1_desc: The Yokosuka P1Y Ginga was a fast bomber capable of making torpedo attacks.
english.ad_aichi_s1a_equipment_1_desc: The Aichi S1A Denko was a purpose built night fighter built to counter the night bombing raids on Japan.
english.ad_kawanishi_n1k4a_equipment_1_desc: The Kawanishi N1K4-A was a carrier capable version developed from the N1K4-J.
english.ad_kawanishi_n1k4j_equipment_1_desc: The Kawanishi N1K4-J was a land-based fighter designed for the Japanese Navy. It was developed from the N1K2-J as a higher-performance variant.
english.ad_kawasaki_ki_100_equipment_1_desc: The Kawasaki Ki-100 was an attempt to install a different engine into the Ki-61-II KAI airframe when the intended engine encountered issues. The result was an aircraft that was almost as fast, but much more reliable, maneuverable, and easier to fly.
english.ad_mitsubishi_a7m2_equipment_1_desc: The Mitsubishi A7M2 Reppu was a carrier fighter aircraft.
english.ad_mitsubishi_j8m_equipment_1_desc: The Mitsubishi Ki-200/J8M was a rocket interceptor based on the German Me 163.
english.ad_mitsubishi_ki_83_equipment_1_desc: The Mitsubishi Ki-83 was designed as a long range heavy fighter. The design was a response to a 1943 specification for a new heavy fighter with great range. The first of four prototypes flew on 18 November 1944.
english.ad_nakajima_ki_84_equipment_2_desc: The Nakajima Ki-84b was designed as an all-purpose fighter.
english.ad_nakajima_kikka_equipment_1_desc: The Nakajima Kikka was a jet attacker inspired by the German Me 262. One prototype was flown, with 19 others in various stages of production when the war ended.
english.ad_rikugun_ki_93_equipment_1_desc: The Rikugun Ki-93 was designed to be a heavy fighter armed with large calibre cannon to serve in the anti-shipping or bomber destroyer roles
english.ad_yokosuka_p1_gb_equipment_1_desc: This is a version of the P1Y designed to carry the Ohka, a manned suicide missile.
english.ad_kawasaki_ki91_equipment_1_desc: Heavy Bombers are designed to perform long-range bombing missions on strategic targets.
english.ad_kyushu_j7w_equipment_1_desc: The Kyushu J7W1 was a land-based fighter designed for the Japanese Navy. It was of an unusual design, with the propellor situated at the rear of the aircraft. Two prototypes were completed, but mass production was halted by the end of the war.
english.ad_nakajima_ki_201_equipment_1_desc: The Nakajima Ki-201 was a jet fighter based more closely on the German Me 262.
english.ad_tachikawa_ki_94_equipment_1_desc: The Tachikawa Ki-94-II was a late war high-altitude interceptor prototype.
english.ad_engine_inline_1_1x_desc: A liquid-cooled inline aircraft engine of simple construction and modest production cost.
english.ad_engine_inline_2_1x_desc: A liquid-cooled inline aircraft engine of simple construction and modest production cost.
english.ad_engine_inline_3_1x_desc: A liquid-cooled inline aircraft engine of simple construction and modest production cost.
english.ad_engine_inline_4_1x_desc: A liquid-cooled inline aircraft engine of simple construction and modest production cost.
english.ad_mg17_2x_desc: 7.92×57mm belt-fed closed-bolt aircraft machine gun suitable for synchronized firing through the propeller arc.
english.ad_mg81_2x_desc: 7.92×57mm belt-fed single-barrel machine gun developed for high rates of fire in aircraft installations.
english.ad_mg81z_1x_desc: Twin-barrel 7.92×57mm MG 81 installation delivering an exceptionally high combined rate of fire, also used in the Gießkanne six-gun underwing pod.
english.ad_mg131_2x_desc: 13×64mm B heavy aircraft machine gun capable of firing high-explosive and incendiary ammunition.
english.ad_mg15115_2x_desc: 15×96mm heavy aircraft machine gun with high muzzle velocity and strong armor penetration.
english.ad_cannon_mg_ff_desc: Early drum-fed 20×80mm RB aircraft cannon fitted in the wings of single-engine fighters and the noses of twin-engine destroyers.
english.ad_cannon_mg_ff_m_desc: Improved MG FF modified to fire thin-walled Minengeschoss high-explosive shells.
english.ad_cannon_mg_151_20_desc: Belt-fed 20×82mm aircraft cannon serving as the primary Luftwaffe fighter armament.
english.ad_cannon_mg_c_30_l_desc: Experimental high-velocity 20×138mm B motor-mounted aircraft cannon.
english.ad_cannon_mg_204_desc: 20×105mm flexible aircraft cannon mounted in defensive turrets on German flying boats.
english.ad_cannon_mk_101_desc: High-velocity 30×184mm B anti-tank gun pod cannon capable of penetrating the side and rear armor of heavy tanks.
english.ad_cannon_mk_103_desc: Improved belt-fed 30×184mm B heavy cannon suitable for both motor-cannon and gun-pod installations.
english.ad_cannon_mk_108_desc: Compact 30×90mm RB autocannon firing heavy high-explosive shells, standard armament on late-war interceptors, night fighters, and jets.
english.ad_cannon_bk_37_desc: 37×263mm B heavy anti-tank aircraft cannon carried in underwing gun pods.
english.ad_cannon_bk_5_desc: 50×420mm R heavy aircraft cannon fed from a 21-round semicircular magazine for anti-bomber and anti-armor roles.
english.ad_cannon_bk_75_desc: 75mm anti-tank aircraft cannon derived from the Pak 40, the largest-caliber gun fitted to Luftwaffe ground-attack aircraft.
english.ad_mg15_2x_desc: 7.92×57mm flexible defensive machine gun fed from a 75-round saddle drum, widely used across bomber crew stations.
english.ad_defense_mg17_2x_desc: 7.92×57mm MG 17 machine guns adapted for flexible defensive mounts.
english.ad_defense_mg81_2x_desc: 7.92×57mm belt-fed MG 81 machine guns in flexible nose, dorsal, and ventral defensive stations.
english.ad_defense_mg81z_1x_desc: Twin-barrel 7.92×57mm MG 81Z installation in rear, ventral Bola, and tail defensive positions.
english.ad_defense_mg131_2x_desc: 13×64mm B MG 131 heavy machine guns in dorsal, nose, powered turret, and remotely controlled defensive mounts.
english.ad_defense_mg15115_2x_desc: 15×96mm MG 151/15 heavy machine guns in forward-facing powered defensive turrets.
english.ad_defense_mg_ff_desc: 20×80mm RB MG FF cannon in flexible defensive mounts on bombers and flying boats.
english.ad_defense_mg_151_20_desc: 20×82mm MG 151/20 cannon in nose, tail, and ventral Bola defensive mounts.
english.ad_engine_argus_as_10_1x_desc: Air-cooled inverted V8 introduced by Argus in 1928, with roughly 28,700 units built.
english.ad_engine_argus_as_410_1x_desc: Air-cooled inverted V12 aircraft engine introduced by Argus in 1937.
english.ad_engine_bmw_vi_1x_desc: Liquid-cooled V12 introduced by BMW in 1926; over 9,200 were built through 1938, continuing in trainer and reconnaissance service into the early war.
english.ad_engine_bmw_132_1x_desc: Nine-cylinder radial developed by BMW from the Pratt & Whitney Hornet license, with over 21,000 units produced.
english.ad_engine_bmw_801_1x_desc: Germany's most-produced radial aircraft engine with over 61,000 units built, pioneering fan-assisted cooling and single-lever Kommandogerät engine control.
english.ad_engine_bramo_322_1x_desc: Formerly the Siemens-Halske Sh 22, derived from the licensed Bristol Jupiter and plagued by chronic reliability problems.
english.ad_engine_bramo_323_1x_desc: Known as the Fafnir, with about 5,500 built; improved upon the 322 with fuel injection and an upgraded supercharger.
english.ad_engine_db_600_1x_desc: First of Daimler-Benz's inverted V12 family; 2,281 were built between 1936 and 1938 before being superseded by the DB 601.
english.ad_engine_db_601_1x_desc: Fuel-injected evolution of the DB 600, with roughly 19,000 engines produced.
english.ad_engine_db_603_1x_desc: Enlarged derivative of the DB 601 entering production in May 1942 with 8,758 units built; the largest-displacement inverted V12 to see German combat service.
english.ad_engine_db_605_1x_desc: Bored-out development of the DB 601 with roughly 42,400 built, hindered by bearing and lubricant reliability issues.
english.ad_engine_db_606_1x_desc: Twin coupled DB 601 engines driving a single reduction gearbox, weighing around 1.5 tonnes and notorious for in-flight engine fires due to inadequate nacelle cooling.
english.ad_engine_db_610_1x_desc: Twin coupled DB 605 powerplant serving as the heart of Germany's only operational heavy bomber.
english.ad_engine_jumo_205_1x_desc: Junkers opposed-piston two-stroke diesel engine with about 900 built; economical for long-range maritime patrol despite sluggish throttle response.
english.ad_engine_jumo_207_1x_desc: High-altitude turbocharged and intercooled derivative of the Jumo 205 (200–300 built), enabling reconnaissance flights above 12 km.
english.ad_engine_jumo_210_1x_desc: Germany's first mass-produced inverted V12 gasoline aircraft engine.
english.ad_engine_jumo_211_1x_desc: Germany's highest-production aircraft engine of the war, with 68,248 units built.
english.ad_engine_jumo_213_1x_desc: Pressurized-cooling, high-RPM development of the Jumo 211 sharing mounting points with the DB 603.
english.ad_engine_jumo_004_1x_desc: The world's first mass-produced axial-flow turbojet with around 8,000 built. Due to nickel and chromium shortages, the 004B used steel turbine blades with an overhaul life of roughly 25 hours.
english.ad_engine_bmw_003_1x_desc: Germany's second mass-produced turbojet with around 3,500 built; lower thrust than the Jumo 004, but smaller in diameter and more fuel-efficient.
english.ad_engine_hwk_509_1x_desc: Hydrogen peroxide / hydrazine-methanol bipropellant liquid rocket motor, throttleable between roughly 300 and 1,700 kgf at the cost of extreme fuel consumption.
english.ad_engine_argus_as_10_2x_desc: Air-cooled inverted V8 introduced by Argus in 1928, with roughly 28,700 units built. Twin-engine installation.
english.ad_engine_argus_as_10_4x_desc: Air-cooled inverted V8 introduced by Argus in 1928, with roughly 28,700 units built. Four-engine installation.
english.ad_engine_argus_as_410_2x_desc: Air-cooled inverted V12 aircraft engine introduced by Argus in 1937. Twin-engine installation.
english.ad_engine_argus_as_410_4x_desc: Air-cooled inverted V12 aircraft engine introduced by Argus in 1937. Four-engine installation.

english.ad_engine_bmw_vi_4x_desc: Liquid-cooled V12 introduced by BMW in 1926; over 9,200 were built through 1938, continuing in trainer and reconnaissance service into the early war. Four-engine installation.

english.ad_engine_bmw_132_4x_desc: Nine-cylinder radial developed by BMW from the Pratt & Whitney Hornet license, with over 21,000 units produced. Four-engine installation.

english.ad_engine_bramo_322_4x_desc: Formerly the Siemens-Halske Sh 22, derived from the licensed Bristol Jupiter and plagued by chronic reliability problems. Four-engine installation.

english.ad_engine_db_600_4x_desc: First of Daimler-Benz's inverted V12 family; 2,281 were built between 1936 and 1938 before being superseded by the DB 601. Four-engine installation.

english.ad_engine_db_601_4x_desc: Fuel-injected evolution of the DB 600, with roughly 19,000 engines produced. Four-engine installation.
